chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb or Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Deliver from me such and such regarding matters I have ordered.' I said: 'So I will deliver them from you, and I will say on my own behalf what you said to me, and other than what you said?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, indeed. The reconciler is not a liar; rather, reconciliation is not a lie.'
ai.seo_question: Is a mediator considered a liar when conveying messages with additions for the sake of peace?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the jurisprudential concept of 'as-sulh' (reconciliation) as a legitimate form of communication distinct from 'al-kidhb' (lying), thereby permitting messengers to adapt their wording to suit the context of peace-making. This principle, rooted in Shia scholarly tradition, underscores the ethical flexibility required in social mediation, where the intent of preserving harmony validates minor deviations from literal truth, provided they do not constitute deception.
